Shalom from Galilee,

People often ask me how I can be so alarmed by the current shift in U.S. policy toward Israel while at the same time teach that such developments were predicted in Scripture.

That is an excellent question.

As believers, we are often torn between what we know and what we see. We know the direction in which this fallen world is heading, yet we still grieve over it and resist every attempt to pressure us into becoming part of its rebellion against God.

In the case of the current U.S. administration’s turn against Israel, it hurts even more because it is being carried out by the most pro-Israel president America has ever had.

You may ask, “Amir, what is the point of resisting and speaking out against things that are already foretold?”

This is exactly where we must remember two truths from Scripture.

Although we are in this world, we are not of this world. As our Messiah said:

“They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”

(John 17:16 NKJV)

And Paul wrote:

“And let us not grow weary while doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart.”

(Galatians 6:9 NKJV)

Though we know what God has foretold, we are still called to stand for what is right and not grow weary in doing good.

My dear brothers and sisters, our hearts are going to break many times because of the things we are about to witness in this world.

In fact, neither the rapture nor even our return with the Lord to reign during the thousand-year Kingdom will completely remove the reality of man’s fallen nature. At the end of the greatest theocracy the world will ever know - with Yeshua Himself reigning from Jerusalem - Satan will be released from his prison and will deceive multitudes into joining him in what will become the greatest rebellion in human history.

“Now when the thousand years have expired, Satan will be released from his prison and will go out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle, whose number is as the sand of the sea.”

(Revelation 20:7–8 NKJV)

Yes, our hearts will be broken, and we will shed many tears. But only in the New Jerusalem will we finally enjoy a world free from sin and sorrow.

“And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away.”

(Revelation 21:4 NKJV)

Therefore, let me encourage you to remain gracious and to rejoice in the Lord - not in the world - as we eagerly await our Messiah, who is coming to take us to be with Him.

“Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say, rejoice!”

(Philippians 4:4 NKJV)

And as Paul wrote:

“Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.”

(1 Corinthians 15:58 NKJV)

As we keep

“looking for the blessed hope and glorious appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,”

(Titus 2:13 NKJV)

Awaiting His Return,

Amir

Hormuz as Hostage

Iran just turned the Strait of Hormuz into a live “off” switch for Trump’s miracle peace deal. 

Tehran’s Khatam al‑Anbiya command announced the strait is closed again, accusing the US of breaking its own memorandum by failing to stop Israel from violating the Lebanon cease-fire. 

One night of rocket swaps and airstrikes on southern Lebanon — and the world’s main oil artery gets shut in revenge.

On paper, the US‑Iran preliminary deal was simple: end fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon, restart talks in Switzerland, slowly reopen Hormuz. 

Israel and Hezbollah traded volleys within 24 hours of the last truce, seven Lebanese civilians were reported killed, dozens wounded, and Tehran claimed this “clear breach” justified closing the waterway again. 

The “secondary front” in Lebanon has become the main veto power over the entire war’s endgame.

Washington insists the show goes on. Pakistan says “technical talks” will start Sunday at Bürgenstock; JD Vance tells Fox News his envoys — Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff — are already in Switzerland and ready to bargain, and Iran’s foreign ministry says its team is en route. 

But while diplomats talk about “discreet and reliable” Swiss hospitality, the only thing that really matters for markets is this: ships that had just begun moving more freely through Hormuz are now staring at headlines about closure — again.

Even inside Iran’s system, no one wants to own this mess outright. New supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is already distancing himself from Trump’s memorandum, signaling that any final deal — billions in unfrozen assets, sanction relief, nuclear limits — can still be blamed on “the negotiators” if it turns sour. 

For Trump, it’s worse: his “decisive victory” over Iran now depends on Hezbollah fighters on a Lebanese ridge not shooting too much and the IDF not bombing too aggressively. That’s not hegemony. That’s crisis management by people who lost the remote.

So Hormuz is closed, again — not by storms or pirates, but by a political tantrum built into the deal’s DNA. One side bombs Iran for months, the other side shuts the oil gate every time its Lebanese proxies and Israel clash, and both then pretend they’re inching toward “permanent peace.” 

The war is supposedly ending, but the most important chokepoint on the planet just became the bargaining chip of a government that Washington swears is “finished.”

📡 Pezeshkian: Tehran-Washington understanding largely serves interests of Iranian people

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian says the provisions of the understanding between Iran and the United States are largely in the interests of the Iranian people, adding that negotiations between the two sides will help Iran access its resources and make decisions on how they are used.

Pezeshkian made the remarks at a seminar in Tehran on monetary and banking policies on Sunday, the same day delegations from Iran and the US began talks in Switzerland, four days after Pezeshkian and US President Donald Trump electronically signed a memorandum of understanding that ended the war launched by the US and Israel against Iran in late February.
​
The Iranian delegation, led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Sunday talks in Switzerland are aimed at ensuring the implementation of the MoU, which calls for the cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. Based on the MoU, Iran and the US are holding talks within a 60-day period, which could be extended with mutual consent, to resolve the standoff over Iran’s nuclear program and to lift sanctions against the Islamic Republic.
​
“The provisions of the understanding between Tehran and Washington are largely in the interests of the Iranian people,” President Pezeshkian said, adding that Iran has exported more than 16 million barrels of oil in the past several days.
​
“The achievements of these talks are very clear. We will be able to access our own resources and make our own decisions regarding them,” he said regarding the talks between Iran and the US in Switzerland.
​
“In this short period, we have been able to take many measures. God willing, with the start of the negotiations from today, the $6 billion we have in Qatar will also be unfrozen and returned to our country,” the president noted, adding that the presence of the Governor of the Central Bank of Iran, Abdolnasser Hemmati, in the Swiss talks is aimed at determining in which sectors these resources should be spent and what measures should be taken.
​
Referring to Washington’s position that Iran should not produce atomic weapons, President Pezeshkian said the Islamic Republic has repeatedly stated that it will never seek to produce a nuclear bomb.
​
“This is not a new issue, and it was stated by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution over the past many years,” he said, referring to a religious decree by the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, which bans the production and use of nuclear weapons.
​
Also in his remarks, President Pezeshkian said Israel is unhappy with the current negotiations between Iran and the US. Israel does not want peace to be restored to the region, and its actions in Gaza and Lebanon are in line with that goal, while the regime seeks to prolong the war, he added.
​
Pezeshkian also called for preserving national unity, warning that enemies are seeking to exploit potential internal divisions to achieve their goals.
​
“Any message that carries the scent of division and discord is essentially moving in the same direction as what [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu and the architects of his political strategies are pursuing. We must remain aware and avoid doing anything that would lead us into the trap of division and discord,” the president said.
